dedupe_keys.name: ames wholesale power market test bed agent based simulation of iso managed electricity markets

description: AMES (Agent-based Modeling of Electricity Systems) is an open-source computational laboratory for studying centrally managed wholesale power markets, developed by Leigh Tesfatsion and collaborators at Iowa State University to follow the market design proposed by the U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in 2003: an independent system operator, a two-settlement day-ahead and real-time structure, locational marginal pricing for congestion and market power oversight. Generating companies and load-serving entities are agents, and the model simulates day-ahead and real-time markets with generator learning implemented through a reinforcement learning module and the operator's DC optimal power flow solved by DCOPFJ. The page documents versions V2.07 (Java), V3.0, V4.0 with an eight-zone ISO-NE test system, and V5.0 with an ERCOT test system, with slide sets, manuals and source downloads. Coverage is generic markets with test systems for two U.S. regions. Access: zip downloads and GitHub repositories linked from the page; licence stated for V2.07 is GPL, the software is unsupported and provided as-is, and cost is free. Caveats: research code with a Java 17 toolchain for V2.07, and results depend on the chosen learning and bidding behaviour. It suits market design, market power and grid-integration studies, and pairs with the PSST power system toolbox catalogued here.
